title: UK and EU Close to a Deal for Young Travellers
summary:
Young people in Britain and Europe could soon find it easier to live, work and travel in each other's countries. The UK and the EU are expected to agree a new youth mobility scheme in Brussels on Friday.

The scheme would let the same number of Britons into Europe as Europeans into Britain. The UK already has similar schemes with 13 countries, including Australia, Canada and India.

In 2024, the EU proposed letting 18- to 30-year-olds work or study in the EU and UK for up to four years. Labour said no then, but now in government it says it would consider a more limited scheme.

Two issues have been sticking points: the UK's request to limit numbers, and the EU's request that EU students pay the same tuition fees as British students.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the deal could also bring lower food prices and lower costs for business. A trade agreement could add £5 billion to the economy, the government argues. Not everyone is happy: Kemi Badenoch accused Burnham of 'reopening the divisions' of Brexit.
why_it_matters: If the deal goes ahead, you might one day be able to live, work or study in Europe more easily.

background_read: The UK left the European Union, so Britons and Europeans no longer have an automatic right to live and work in each other's countries.
A youth mobility scheme is a deal that lets young adults spend some time abroad to work, study or travel.
Governments negotiate such deals, and any agreement still needs to become law.
